category_title: Pupils with high SNA dependence and learned helplessness
minimal_context: The student is preparing to start a classroom assignment while the SNA pulls up a chair to sit directly beside his desk.
dialogue:
TUTOR: I am going to pull my chair up right beside your desk so we can do this assignment together.

STUDENT: I don't need you right here. I want to do it like the boys do.

TUTOR: I'm just going to stay right here next to you to make sure you stay on task.

STUDENT: I want to be like everyone else in the class.

TUTOR: We need to get this finished, so I will sit here and help you.

STUDENT: I don't want anyone sitting next to me! I need to have my own space now!

options.A: Teach specific self-regulation strategies, such as going to a quiet place or counting to ten.
options.B: Provide detailed instruction for each specific element of the classroom assignment.
options.C: Employ intermittent support for the student during the classroom assignment.
options.D: Direct the student to take a few minutes to calm down before starting the assignment.
